title: Background Jobs and Task Queues knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Background Jobs and Task Queues?
options: Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Authenticate connections, authorize each event/resource, clean up disconnected clients, and design idempotent job handling.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Authenticate connections, authorize each event/resource, clean up disconnected clients, and design idempotent job handling.
questions.explanation: Authenticate connections, authorize each event/resource, clean up disconnected clients, and design idempotent job handling. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Background Jobs and Task Queues?
questions.explanation: “Job producers and workers” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Background Jobs and Task Queues implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
